item.title: We modify designs to fit real world usage. Sometimes we engage in hundreds of hours of discussion and work just so that something becomes simpler on the surface. Case in point: the recent v2 releases radically simplified end-to-end encryption. No more lock icons or special encryption UI elements because everything is encrypted by default. Even better, the amount of security sensitive code was reduced, making #chatmail code bases easier to audit and maintain.

What if a state tries to mandate us as #deltachat app devs/distributors to shut down a chat profile? Nothing. It can't be done. We have no list of chat identities, have no handle or data about them, and don't mediate the message transfer. However, EU #Chatcontrol politicians and Russian authorities would want us to insert backdoors into our FOSS code. But that is nothing than can happen overnight, and we are fine with friendly forks already. Resilient private internet communication ftw :)

Delta Chat is hard to classify when your question is violently binary. Federated or P2P? #deltachat is more P2P than #Briar in that we implement a P2P group model while Briar routes everything through a central administrator who owns the group. E2EE Messenger or e-mail? #chatmail relays are aiming to be like Signal servers in many ways, but are based on IETF standards around TLS, OpenPGP, MIME, SMTP etc., stripping them all down to the core that we actually need. Quite fun :)

Woah! Only now did we discover a great blog post from @wq who discusses the progression from hosting a #Matrix , a #Snikket and a #SimpleX server, to now running a #chatmail relay https://runtimeterror.dev/self-hosted-chatmail-relay-for-delta-chat/ It's an excellent read, with lots of good advise, including having a public "hello" profile and another unpublished chat profile for private chatting. #deltachat apps have pervasive multi-profile support (and multi-device support) so it's pretty easy to establish such a two-profile setup.

#deltachat is being used in virtually all world regions where one or more other messengers fail to work. We recently released a major milestone (V2 security hardening releases) that prepared the ground for chat profiles to have multiple #chatmail relays at once ... failure or blocking of a single relay would not disrupt chatting anymore. But multi transport also helps with the "centralization problem in decentralized systems" ... https://delta.chat/en/2025-06-04-surge-donations#funding-for-a-globally-scaled-chatmail-relay-network (Funding is looking good currently btw!)

When we are interviewing we typically ask about experience in collectively working and p2p collaboration .... It doesn't need to be about contributing to collective open source projects, but political or youth organizing or working in grassroots movements, is significant as well. Why do we ask for this? Because collectivity needs learning it. Our work involves overlapping, sometimes controversial discussions, and involves many from partnering projects and user groups across the globe.

We are in a continuous process to better understand what we are doing, and often gain new understandings :) Among the papers discussed regarding UX (user experience) is a still interesting text from 2012 about "the manufactured normalcy field" from Venkatesh Rao https://www.ribbonfarm.com/2012/05/09/welcome-to-the-future-nauseous/ It's interesting to relate it to mainstream messaging Whatsapp style which really evolved from contact based texting (sms) etc ...

Sometimes we are surprised ourselves how well everything works :) - cross-platform #deltachat releases every 2-3 months, with a focus on never breaking the world despite significant underlying changes - many #chatmail relays humming along, including the default onboarding one serving 230K monthly users with ~0 admin hours needed -lively and sometimes controversial discussions among the diverse dozen core contributors, with an evolving shared vision, both short and long term Toi Toi Toi

#Whatsapp on #iOS had a severe 0day that was exploited in the wild for some months, and is fixed with august 20th releases https://hackread.com/whatsapp-0-day-exploit-attack-targeted-ios-macos-users/ Last year #signal also had its multi-device functionality exploited in the wild. https://thehackernews.com/2025/02/hackers-exploit-signals-linked-devices.html FWIW #deltachat has a dumber multi-device sync model, no device linking, depends on being in the same WiFI for setup (therefore no easy remote exploits), and #OpenPGP signatures and verification for ongoing usage (like all other E2EE messages).

While most of the feedback on the #deltachat V2 releases has been positive, some users sense a de-prioritization of "classic unencrypted email" usage. Indeed the current dozen or so contributors aim to evolve an exceptionally resilient and versatile private messenger app suite, with end-to-end encryption the primary focus and design foundation. However, we would support friendly forkers to develop a classic e-mail focused app suite -- say "deltamail" (work title). What do you think? Nah, just use Thunderbird and call it a day Yes, deltamail apps on all platforms please! Give up messenger effort, focus on classic email Something else (feel free to reply)

As far as we know #deltachat supports the widest range of old mobile devices. And it's real often hard work to achieve that. For example, on android three (!) rust/networking experts needed to huddle for many days to sort out "how to get own device IP addresses". They ended up implementing several mechanisns suitable for respective android versions. It became part of the @n0iroh network rust stack that powers Delta's integrated peer-to-peer #webxdc realtime networking.

As with the demise of windows10, various meta happenings around Whatsapp open possibilities to welcome refugees. Instead of blaming them for not having had whatever insights earlier, there are often just very practical questions where a helping hand does wonders. Offering help instead of trying to convince. Currently many companies are giving win11-incompatible laptops away, often powerful systems that deserve upgrading to Linux, and then donating then. It also helps to counter hardware waste.

What are the main obstacles for you to adopt usage of #deltachat apps with your families, friends or communities? if you have other issues than the poll options please add to the replies. Oh, and those who are also living through heat waves: stay hydrated, and remind everyone else :) can't get my folks to install another app lack of audio/video calls lack of Sealed-Sender/PQC/Forward-secrecy haven't used it (enough) myself yet

The UK's national drought group is falling ridiculously short when recommending to delete old emails. How about - stop building any new data centers, progressively tax on their size and resource consumption, no free riding - legislatively focus on software to become more resource efficient (hint: AI hurts not helps with that) In any case, #chatmail relays unconditionally remove emails, no user action needed. Everything interesting happens on end devices see https://en.reset.org/decentralised-efficient-without-being-addictive-delta-chat-is-our-favourite-instant-messenger/

We are impressed with the new https://fightchatcontrol.eu/ website, and the way it provides all the info needed to engage in distributed diverse action to prevent the EU from preparing the ground for, or sliding into, authoritarianism by breaking end-to-end encryption for everyone. Germany and France are particularly important to engage with and we'll see what we can do from our circles. We don't know the people behind @chatcontrol but big kudos! #chatcontrol

@cross do you need an ai summary of your family and private friends or small community groups? Having such summaries for joining pubpic groups with anonymous onboarding is easier to see a potential use in. Anyways, if you have a good example to point to for use of ai in private chatting, we would be happy to hear it. thanks.

@kleines_z today, there are larger groups (sometimes 100+ members) but both due to legal and economic reasons we do not emphasize or recommend this usage because moderation tooling is lacking. Also the most severe problems come from admins disagreeing or going to war with each other. Technically fixing this is tricky or impossible. It's not unlikely we will engage in improving mod tooling in the next year and are in fact eying a massively scaling admin-controlled encrypted channel feature.

We do not aim for #deltachat to be another social media app. No #ai summaries or suggestions. No public directory of contacts. No discovery via outside identifiers (mobile phone or email). Just you and your contacts privately messaging, in a solid simple user interface on all platforms. End-to-End encryption enforced on two layers. #chatmail relays know and retain nothing, no content or metadata. #webxdc apps allow for custom interactions on top of chats. Contributors and donations welcome!

Prediction: most messenger projects will move to a single core implementation model, probably #Rust based, in the next few years. The gains both for the development process are just too big. It's all about UI and UX agility, implementation quality and delivery to users. Funding and money? We had/have to make do with ~1/50th of what other cross platform messenger app efforts had available. It forced and forces us to economic choices which is not a bad thing in an overall bloated IT industry.

Now that @fdroidorg also ships v2 releases, roll out to all platforms is complete 😅 and we are curious. How was your v2 experience so far in relation to end-to-end encryption? v2 rocks, no issues or complaints so far v2 caused en/decryption problems (please reply) didn't upgrade to v2 yet still holding off on trying delta out
